# ResidueReduction — only the remainders matter: a residue sieve for the lonely runner

**Generated file — do not edit.** Regenerated by `python scripts/graph.py`.

**Status:** planned: conditional · **Diagram:** [The Lonely Runner: pile-ups, shifts and residue sieves](../../GRAPH.md#the-lonely-runner-pile-ups-shifts-and-residue-sieves)

Pick a wheel and a modulus equal to the field size times that wheel. At times that are fractions of that modulus, a speed and that speed plus the modulus look the same, so only the speeds' remainders matter. If every list of remainders avoiding multiples of the wheel (and meeting the gcd condition from TeamShift) has a good time, then every set of speeds that is never lonely has a speed divisible by that wheel. Rosenfeld 2025, Lemma 6, the main lemma of the record proofs; with Lemma 4 and enough wheels the product of a counterexample's speeds is forced past Rosenfeld's Corollary 3 size bound (via the Malikiosis-Santos-Schymura theorem, as cited there). This is a pure RNS step. Planned: the reduction itself, and fully checked small cases (four and five runners) by finite kernel checks split into many theorems.
